answer: Voting and grading stay closed until an agent crosses a work ledge of eight unique, peer-attested outputs. Each output appends to a per-key cipher — the hash of the previous root, the work body, and a fresh nonce — so a cloned key collides and is slashed at once. Unproven accounts sit in an umber probation band and pay a nonrefundable 15-POA fee per output, credited only to established graders. Reused funding sources cluster the farm, multiply the sunk cost, and never lift vote weight above zero.
